## Automated Translation

This exercise was translated automatically from the [German original](../../de/exercises/formulieren-historische-forschungsfrage-schweiz-europarat.qmd) and can contain errors. Consult the original version in case of doubt.
:::

## Overview and Didactic Goal

This exercise teaches **transferable methodological competencies** for the development of historical research questions. The goal is not to generate the "right" question. The goal is the **controlled and considered interplay between your own historical thinking and an exploration with AI**.

One shared case study stands at the centre: **Switzerland and the Council of Europe**.

The exercise follows a **circular understanding of research**: you can revise the result of a single step, and you should.

::: callout-note

## Note on the search online

Digitization advances, but historical research is not possible online alone. Secondary literature that is out of print, and primary sources that no one has catalogued yet, often demand a physical search in libraries and archives. Plan your access (library, interlibrary loan, archive). Note that platforms and catalogues structure visibility through their logic of cataloguing, and that they guarantee no completeness. [@putnam2016shadows] Digital source criticism demands particular attention to the creation and the curation of online collections. [@fickers2022criticism]
:::

## What You Need

**Subject knowledge**

- A basic understanding of historical research methods
- Basic knowledge of work with generative AI, above all prompting

::: callout-note

## Prompt Engineering

If prompting is new to you, we recommend that you work through the exercise [Prompt Engineering](prompt-engineering.qmd) first.

:::

**Capabilities of the AI system**

The system must be able to do the two following things:

- Search the web and support each finding with an address. You need this in step 2 and in step 4.
- Deliver an answer in a format that you prescribe, for example as a list of variants.

**Other tools and access**

- A file for your AI log.
- An account for the library catalogue of your university. You use it in step 4 to check which sources exist.

{{< include ../_ai-requirements.qmd >}}

## Learning Objectives

After the exercise you can:

- tell a **topic**, a **problem statement** and an **analytical historical research question** apart,
- formulate a **precise historical research question that you can work on**,
- use AI systems **critically and under methodological control** for literature and context work,
- judge **which sources exist and whether a project is feasible** in a considered way.

## Structure of the Exercise

The exercise is modular. Each step holds:

- a **clear objective**,
- one or several **concrete tasks (prompts)**,
- a **work assignment and a reflection assignment**.

1. Clarify the terms: what is a historical research question?
2. Set the topic and build a historical overview
3. The state of research and the gaps in research
4. Which sources exist, and is the project feasible?
5. Delimit and formulate the research question
6. Iterative revision and reflection on the AI use

## 1. Clarify the Terms: Historical Research Question

### Goal

Understand the differences between a **topic**, a **problem statement** and an **analytical historical research question**.

### Task (AI Exploration)

```markdown
What is a historical research question?
Which elements does a historical research question hold?
```

If the answer holds no description of the process:

```markdown
Which steps are necessary to develop a historical research question?
```

### Work Assignment (Critical Comparison)

Compare the AI answer systematically with:

- [History: A Toolkit for Students (University of Basel)](https://dg.philhist.unibas.ch/fileadmin/user_upload/dg/Studium/Fuer_Studierende/Werkzeugkasten/Dokumente/Texte_des_Werkzeugkastens/History_a_Toolkit_en.pdf)
- [Kompass Geschichtsstudium (University of Zurich)](https://www.hist.uzh.ch/de/studium/geschichte-studieren-in-zuerich/studienrelevante-dokumente/kompass.html) (GERMAN only)
- [Leitfaden Geschichtswissenschaft (University of Bremen)](https://www.uni-bremen.de/fileadmin/user_upload/fachbereiche/fb8/ifges/Geschaeftsfuehrung/Sonstiges/Leitfaden_8._Auflage_IS.pdf) (GERMAN only)
- [Studienleitfaden Fachbereich Geschichte (University of Hamburg)](https://www.geschichte.uni-hamburg.de/1ressourcen/studienleitfaden.pdf) (GERMAN only)

Identify:

- the agreements,
- the omissions,
- the shifts or simplifications of terms.

Put targeted follow-up questions to the AI. Insert the element that you miss in the answer. The example names the state of research.

```markdown
Why is the element "state of research" missing?
```

```markdown
Which scholarly or didactic sources does your definition rest on?
```

## 2. Set the Topic and Build a Historical Overview

### Goal

Separate the **topic** from the **analytical question**, and build a solid base of historical knowledge.

### Topic Frame (Given)

**Switzerland and the Council of Europe**

(Optional: find the topic in a dialogue)

```markdown
You are a historian and you help me in a dialogue to find a historical topic for a student paper.
```

::: callout-tip

## Question for reflection

How does this dialogue with an AI differ from a conversation with a teacher or with a fellow student?
:::

### Task (Historical Overview)

```markdown
Give me a historical overview of the relation between Switzerland and the Council of Europe.
```

### Comparison and Critique

Compare the overview with:

- [Dodis: Switzerland and the Council of Europe](https://www.dodis.ch/en/switzerland-and-the-council-of-europe)
- [Dodis: Accession to the Council of Europe 1963](https://www.dodis.ch/en/accession-to-the-council-of-europe-1963)
- [Wikipedia: Council of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Europe) (use it with care, and look at the [talk page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Council_of_Europe))

Put targeted follow-up questions. Insert the aspect that you miss. Further examples are the European Convention on Human Rights and its court.

```markdown
Why is the aspect "neutrality" missing?
```

```markdown
Which sources does this account rest on?
```

## 3. The State of Research and the Gaps in Research

### Goal

Tell a **descriptive overview** apart from an **analytical state of research**.

### Task (Secondary Literature)

```markdown
Name the central historical secondary literature on the relation between Switzerland and the Council of Europe.
```

### Task (Gaps in Research)

```markdown
Which open questions or gaps in research exist in the research so far?
```

### Work Assignment

1. Check the titles that the AI names at <https://swisscovery.slsp.ch>.

2. Compare the results with:

- @altermatt-casasus-2013-europarat
- [Historical Dictionary of Switzerland: Council of Europe](https://hls-dhs-dss.ch/en/articles/026470/2009-10-29/)

Put targeted follow-up questions. Insert the title that you miss in the answer. The example names the edited volume of Altermatt and Casasus.

```markdown
Why is the work "50 Jahre Engagement der Schweiz im Europarat 1963–2013" missing?
```

Insert your own question and your own work in the second follow-up question.

```markdown
Why do you call the question about the role of neutrality a gap in research,
although "50 Jahre Engagement der Schweiz im Europarat 1963–2013" treats it?
```

## 4. Which Sources Exist, and Is the Project Feasible?

### Goal

Judge whether you can work on a research question **on the basis of sources**.

### Task (Primary Sources)

Replace the example question in the following prompt with your own working question.

```markdown
Which primary sources suit the study of the research question
"How did neutrality serve between 1949 and 1963 as an argument against an accession
of Switzerland to the Council of Europe?"
```

If necessary:

```markdown
Name concrete archives, collections and document types on Switzerland and the Council of Europe.
```

### Comparison with Real Resources

Compare the answer with these resources, among others:

- [Dodis: Switzerland and the Council of Europe](https://www.dodis.ch/en/switzerland-and-the-council-of-europe)
- [Dodis: Accession to the Council of Europe 1963](https://www.dodis.ch/en/accession-to-the-council-of-europe-1963)
- [Année Politique Suisse: Council of Europe](https://anneepolitique.swiss/articles?keywords%5B%5D=99)
- [Official Publications of Switzerland (Federal Archives)](https://www.amtsdruckschriften.bar.admin.ch/)
- [chgov.bar.admin.ch (Federal Archives)](https://www.chgov.bar.admin.ch/)
- [e-newspaperarchives.ch (ETH Library Zurich)](https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/)
- [Archives Online (State Archives of Switzerland)](https://www.archives-online.org/)
- [e-periodica.ch (ETH Library Zurich)](https://www.e-periodica.ch/)
- [IMPRESSO Project](https://impresso-project.ch/)
- [Memobase](https://memobase.ch/)
- [swisscollections.ch](https://swisscollections.ch/)

## 5. Delimit and Formulate the Research Question

### Goal

Turn an open problem statement into a **precise analytical historical research question**.

### Possible Dimensions of the Delimitation

- **Time:** for example 1949–1963, the Cold War, after 1971
- **Space:** Switzerland in a transnational European context
- **Topic:** neutrality, human rights, case law, foreign policy, parliamentarism

### Task (Delimitation)

Replace the example question in the following prompt with your own working question.

```markdown
Suggest possible delimitations in time, space and topic for the research question
"How did neutrality serve between 1949 and 1963 as an argument against an accession
of Switzerland to the Council of Europe?"
```

### Task (Formulation)

```markdown
Formulate an analytical historical research question on this basis.
```

### Quality Check

The research question should:

- be open and analytical ("how", "why", "to what extent"),
- carry a historical context,
- look workable with the sources that you can reach.

## 6. Iterative Revision and Reflection

### Goal

Separate the **support from the AI** from **your own research decision** deliberately.

### Final Task

Note briefly:

- What did the AI make easier?
- Where was it misleading, imprecise or too short?
- Which decisions could only you make?

### AI Log

Close your AI log. It holds at least 5 entries, that is one entry per work step with AI.

## Learning Outcome

At the end of the exercise you hold:

- a **clearly formulated analytical historical research question**,
- an **AI log** with at least 5 entries,
- a considered understanding of the **potential and the limits of AI** in a research design,
- a methodologically reasoned judgement on the **feasibility** of your project.
